newsitem.title: HONG KONG: HKMA takes HK$1.5 bln out from interbank market.
newsitem.headline: HKMA takes HK$1.5 bln out from interbank market.

text.p: The Hong Kong Monetary Authority (HKMA), the territory's de facto central bank, said on Monday it had extracted HK$1.5 billion from the interbank market in view of softer money market rates on easier demand.
"It's mainly because interbank rates moved lower and demand for Hong Kong dollars is easier, so we extracted HK$1.5 billion from the market," a HKMA spokesman said.
The overnight rate stood at 4-13/16 percent before the extraction, which took place at 15:00 pm (0700 gmt), he said.
The overnight edged a touch higher to 4-7/8 3/4 percent after the action, dealers said.
This is the first fund extraction since HKMA injected a total of about HK$3.0 billion in three interventions last week aimed at soothing tightness caused by month-end and equities-related demand.
